# Admin security: Tickets — workflow, notes and shared right-panel slot

- **Kind**: feature
- **Date**: 2026-08-05
- **Requested by**: Ian
- **Parent**: #1283 "Admin security operations — incidents, events, tickets and rules (epic)"
- **Apply rules**: nativemojo-board-conventions

## Description

Build the ticket workflow used to escalate and collaborate on security work, including editable ticket tables, record-scoped notes and a persistent shared right-side panel shell.

## Context

RecordFeed ticket adapters and the reusable drawer exist. The panel becomes an application-level shell slot that later Assistant work can reuse, while keeping ticket permissions and route state explicit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Ticket table/detail support useful status/category/assignment workflows and record-scoped notes against verified endpoints.
- [ ] An accessible right-panel shell slot opens ticket content, preserves route context, closes predictably and is reusable.
- [ ] Inline edits reject visibly and reconcile TanStack Query caches correctly.
- [ ] Notes reuse RecordFeed; no duplicate conversation framework.
- [ ] Mock parity, component docs/demo where required, focused tests, both themes and keyboard/console/typecheck checks pass.

## Investigation

- **What exists**: RecordFeed, ticket adapters, Modal drawer, ModalManager and global shell.
- **What changes**: ticket models/pages/panel integration and a small reusable shell-slot API.
- **Constraints**: gate launcher and content; native dialog/drawer accessibility; no hidden mutable panel singleton.
- **Port sources**: `web-mojo/src/extensions/admin/incidents/TicketTablePage.js`, `TicketView.js`, `TicketPanelView.js`.
- **Out of scope**: Assistant implementation (#1299) and general chat.

## Plan

### Objective

Ship a permission-gated Tickets workspace at `security/tickets` with server-driven list/search/filter/export, inline status/category changes, create/edit/assignment workflows, record-scoped notes, structured approval cards, Maestro-link visibility, and an application-level right-panel slot. The slot remains mounted across route changes without changing the current route, is React-controlled rather than singleton-driven, and is reusable by #1299 Assistant.

### Verified contracts and scope corrections

- `Ticket` and `TicketNote` are live at `/api/incident/ticket` and `/api/incident/ticket/note`.
- Ticket view is `view_security | security`; create/update/actions are `manage_security | security`; delete is `manage_security`. Admin UI gates must use system-pinned equivalents.
- Ticket actions are `enable_llm`, `disable_llm`, and asynchronous `push_to_maestro`.
- Ticket default graph expands `assignee`, `incident`, `user`, and `group`; it does **not** include web-mojo’s assumed `note_count` or any Maestro link. Do not render a fake note count; query `/api/incident/maestro/item-link?ticket=<id>` separately.
- Ticket status/category are unconstrained strings in django-mojo. Preserve web-mojo’s known choices, add `paused`, `llm_review`, and `assistant_review`, and render an unknown current value rather than blanking or coercing it.
- Ticket status saves create a structured status-change note as a side effect. Every ticket mutation must invalidate the ticket list/detail keys and the exact ticket-feed prefix.
- `TicketNote` creation is tenant-sensitive. Build the adapter from the ticket’s actual `group.id` when present so list and create retain identical scope.
- Approval actions live on `TicketNote.metadata.action`. A response is a new note with `metadata.action_response`; the backend trusts the response context. The UI must copy the pending action’s `handler` and `context` unchanged, never reconstruct or edit them.
- A linked Maestro item is read through `/api/incident/maestro/item-link`; `push_to_maestro` only queues work, so the UI must say “queued” and not pretend the link exists immediately.
- The shipped `modal.drawer()` is transient/modal and intentionally distinct from this persistent shell slot.
- File attachments remain out of scope until #1264.

### Implementation

1. **Add the minimal reusable shell-panel API.**
   - Create `packages/portal-mojo/src/ui/RightPanel.tsx`.
   - Export `RightPanelProvider`, `RightPanelSlot`, `useRightPanel`, and the descriptor/context types from `packages/portal-mojo/src/ui/index.ts`.
   - Keep state in the provider as one explicit descriptor: stable `key`, accessible title/label, and `render({ close })`. `open()` replaces an existing descriptor atomically; `close()` is idempotent.
   - Capture the active launcher on open, focus the panel close control/heading after mount, and restore focus on close when the launcher is still connected.
   - Render a non-modal `<aside role="complementary" aria-labelledby=…>` with a visible close button. Escape closes only when no native dialog is open, avoiding conflicts with `ModalHost`; no focus trap, backdrop, global mutable stack, persisted content, or assistant-specific width behavior.
   - Keep panel selection session-local and out of the hash query. This preserves the current route and avoids leaking `panel` parameters through the table params store into Django lookups.
   - Add panel state/layout CSS in new matching `apps/portal/src/theme/right-panel.css` and `apps/showcase/src/theme/right-panel.css`, imported by both theme aggregators. Use a third grid column on wide layouts and a fixed non-modal aside on narrow layouts; use tokens, safe overflow, reduced-motion handling, and no visual-only close affordance.

2. **Mount the slot once at the application shell.**
   - Update `apps/portal/src/App.tsx` so `RightPanelProvider` wraps an inner shell component; the inner shell reads `isOpen`, applies the open layout class, and renders `RightPanelSlot` as a sibling of `.main`.
   - Keep `ModalHost` and `ToastHost` outside the panel content but inside the provider-backed application tree.
   - Confirm `<Outlet>` remounts do not affect provider state: sidebar navigation changes the main route while the ticket panel remains open; opening another ticket replaces the panel; closing returns focus without navigating.

   - Define a read-only `MaestroItemLinkModel` on `/api/incident/maestro/item-link`.

4. **Build ticket create/edit and inline mutation surfaces.**

     - markdown description;

Stop propagation so an edit does not open the panel; disable while pending; keep the server value until success; render a local `role="alert"` plus toast on rejection; invalidate ticket/feed keys on success.
   - Preserve arbitrary server values by appending the current unknown value to the select. Never silently replace it with a catalog default.

5. **Build the Tickets table.**
   - Extend `ModelTable`/`useTableParams` with a backward-compatible `defaultParams` (or `defaultFilters`) input so route defaults such as `status__in` participate in the one URL-backed params state. Preserve URL > persisted > defaults precedence and document/test it; do not hide defaults in model normalization.
   - In `TicketsPage`, use `ModelTable<TicketRow>` with:
     - default `status__in=new,open` and sort `-priority`;

   - Use badges/dots and priority emphasis from the web-mojo source without trusted HTML.
   - A focusable button in the title cell calls `useRightPanel().open()` with key `ticket:<id>` and passes its exact launcher element for focus restoration; pointer-only row activation is not the keyboard contract. It does not alter the hash route.
   - Do not add batch delete or generic table-cell editing.

6. **Build authoritative panel detail and workflows.**
   - `TicketPanel` fetches by ID with `TicketModel.useOne`; never trusts the sparse list row after opening.
   - Render load/error/retry states and close safely if the ticket is deleted or becomes inaccessible.
   - Header/detail includes title, ID, timestamps, status, priority, category, assignee, group, description through `MarkdownView`, LLM-enabled state, linked incident summary, and existing Maestro item link.
   - View-only users receive a fully readable panel/feed with no inert mutation controls.
   - Manage users get controlled status, priority, category, description, assignee, enable/disable LLM, close-ticket, and push-to-Maestro actions. Each mutation awaits rejection, surfaces failure, and invalidates ticket/feed/link keys as applicable.
   - Assignment requires both ticket-manage and user-view permission; otherwise show the current assignee read-only.
   - For linked incidents, show a bounded reference now; do not create a dead route before #1414. #1414 can enhance it to an incident panel/link.
   - Query Maestro item links by `ticket=<id>, size=1, graph=default`; render `remote_url` only after scheme validation (`https:`/`http:`), otherwise show the remote item ID as text.
   - `push_to_maestro` is unavailable when already linked, confirms before queueing, reports “queued”, and starts bounded polling while queued-and-unlinked (with an explicit manual “Check for link” fallback). Stop on link, timeout, close or error; do not promise immediate completion.

7. **Compose notes and structured approvals through RecordFeed.**
   - Build `createTicketNoteAdapter(ticket.id, { groupId })` from the authoritative ticket.
   - Render `<RecordFeed variant="compact" showInput={canManage}>` for ordinary/status/assistant notes; view-only users get no inert composer. Do not create another composer or conversation cache.
   - Supply `renderAddon` with a `TicketActionCard` that reads `item.metadata.action`.
   - Render only recognized structural fields; unknown handlers remain visible as generic actions rather than disappearing.
   - Disable Approve/Deny when the action is resolved, the ticket is `closed`/`resolved`, the caller lacks manage permission, or a response is pending.
   - Confirm the decision, then POST a new note directly to `/api/incident/ticket/note` with `parent`, ticket group scope, a human-readable note, and:
     `metadata.action_response = { handler: action.handler, action: 'approve'|'deny', context: action.context }`.
   - Copy the source `context` verbatim through the pure helper. Do not expose a JSON editor or allow callers to substitute a target.
   - On success, invalidate the exact feed and ticket/link keys so the resolved stamp, terminal ticket state, and backend-generated system notes repaint. On failure, keep the card actionable and show a local alert/toast.
   - Keep note editing, attachments, Assistant chat, and arbitrary reference navigation out of scope.

### Design decisions

- The panel is provider-controlled session state, not URL query state. This preserves the active route and prevents panel keys from becoming backend table filters.
- The panel is non-modal and complementary. The drawer remains the transient modal choice.
- Ticket-specific inline cells avoid expanding `ModelTable` with a premature generic editing API.
- Approval responses bypass `RecordFeedAdapter.addNote(text)` only for the structured POST, then invalidate RecordFeed’s exact query key. The generic adapter contract stays unchanged.
- Unknown statuses/categories are preserved and editable; django-mojo does not enforce web-mojo’s catalogs.
- One `SECURITY_OPERATIONS_ADMIN_SECTION` owns `/security`; sibling items extend it.

### Edge cases and error handling

- Opening the same ticket is idempotent; opening another replaces content without briefly restoring focus.
- Closing twice, Escape plus button races, and unmounted launchers are harmless.
- An open native dialog consumes Escape before the panel.
- A ticket deleted or permission-revoked while open shows a fail-closed error and closes on request.
- Relation values may be nested objects, IDs, or null.
- Status saves generate notes; invalidating only Ticket caches is insufficient.
- Empty/invalid Maestro URLs never become clickable.
- Assignment lookup failure does not block other ticket management.
- Push-to-Maestro success means queued, not linked.
- Approval replay is blocked in UI but remains server-authoritative.
- Approval cards never execute unrecognized client-side handlers.
- RecordFeed group scope follows the ticket, not any product portal’s active-group context.
- Attachment/media data remains raw and unrendered.

### Challenge

- **Amended:** Encoding panel state in the hash query would preserve reloads but pollute the table params store and backend lookups. The plan uses explicit provider state and leaves the route untouched.
- **Amended:** A generic `RecordFeedAdapter.addNote(text, metadata)` expansion was unnecessary and widened a shipped contract. Structured approvals use a ticket-specific POST plus exact feed invalidation.
- **Amended:** Approval context is a serious trust boundary because django-mojo executes the response context. A pure helper copies the pending note’s context verbatim; there is no editable JSON or reconstructed target.
- **Amended:** Ticket saves also create feed rows and Maestro sync jobs. All mutation paths invalidate ticket, feed, and relevant link keys.
- **Amended:** A visual overlay with dialog semantics would need a focus trap. The slot remains explicitly non-modal/complementary, with focus entry/restoration and no backdrop.
- **Rebutted:** Reusing `modal.drawer()` would be smaller, but it is awaitable, modal, and unmounts on close; it cannot remain alongside route navigation or serve Assistant’s persistent shell use case.

### Batch challenge disposition

- **Amended — default queue state:** `status__in` must enter the shared URL-backed params store through a first-class defaults API with URL > persisted > defaults precedence.
- **Amended — numeric priority:** SchemaForm does not currently enforce numeric min/max, so the ticket editor owns an explicit controlled integer input.
- **Amended — keyboard launcher:** panel opening uses a focusable title-cell button and captures its element; clickable table rows alone are pointer-only.
- **Amended — note permissions:** `RecordFeed` receives `showInput={canManage}`.
- **Amended — asynchronous Maestro link:** queued/unlinked state uses bounded polling plus manual refresh.
- **Amended — domain styling:** ticket/action-card styles live in dedicated matching Admin Security stylesheets, separate from the shell panel layout.
